text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden spike in 5xx rate for inference-gateway (route: /v1/generate). 5xx from ~0.3% -> 9.2% over the last 6m. Latency p95 jumped to 2.4s. Errors look like 502/504 gateway errors from kv/prefix-cache timeouts. Paginated spike started at ~14:02 UTC. Paging oncall.

jamal: ack I'm on it. paging kv/prefix-cache and gateway owners. grabbing logs and timeline. tagging emily-cs for customer impact.

maya: I'm here, can start digging into prefix-cache metrics. saw a scheduled prefetch/compaction job started about 14:00 in eu-west-1 — could be correlated.

liz: pulling tail of prefix-cache logs now. sample:
```
2026-03-15T14:01:58Z ERROR prefix-cache: eviction storm: freed=0 failure=high
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z WARN kvstore-client: rpc to node-4 timed out after 300ms
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z ERROR gateway: upstream timeout (kv-store) for req_id=abc123
```

alex: sounds like eviction + kv rpc timeouts -> gateway 502s. quick mitigation: flip route to bypass cache for high-traffic routes so gateway hits kv-store directly (slower but avoids eviction thrash), or enable read-through fallback that doesn't wait on cache writes. Can do a feature-flag flip from console. Which do we want first?

ops-runner: if we bypass cache we might increase kv-store load. need to throttle QPS or enable circuit breaker. I can apply a temporary route.override for a subset of traffic (5% canary) and watch.

jamal: start with 5% bypass canary + disable prefetch job. maya, can you stop the scheduled prefetch/compaction? liz, watch eviction rate.

maya: disabling prefetch/compaction now (command executed). patch id: prefetch-disable-20260315. Confirming.

sre-bot: runbook step: when prefix-cache eviction spike -> 1) disable prefetch jobs, 2) enable route bypass canary, 3) increase cache TTL to reduce churn, 4) if kv-store overloaded, enable throttling.

ops-runner: applied bypass canary: POST /admin/routes/override {"route":"/v1/generate","bypass_cache":true,"pct":5} -> 200 OK

alex: also pushing TTL tweak: increasing prefix-cache TTL from 30s -> 120s for hot prefixes. That reduces eviction churn while we investigate compaction behavior.

liz: eviction_count metric before change: 23k/min. after prefetch disabled + TTL bump (10m after) eviction_count -> 1.6k/min. Observed 5xx dropping from 9.2% -> 3.1% in first 5m after actions.

emily-cs: customer impact: top impacted customers (based on error logs): AcmeLabs (chat embeddings timeouts), NumiAI (batch embed jobs), BetaApps (realtime chat). We're sending proactive notes to Acme & NumiAI engineering contacts and opening a high-sev support ticket. CS escalation sent.

jamal: good. ops-runner can you expand bypass from 5% -> 25% for next 10m? we'll monitor kv-store CPU and tail latencies.

ops-runner: expanding bypass to 25% now. Command: POST /admin/routes/override {"route":"/v1/generate","bypass_cache":true,"pct":25} -> 200 OK

sre-bot: alert thresholds: kv-store p95 > 800ms OR cpu>85% -> rollback bypass. Watchlist: node-3 latency and node-4 rpc error rate.

maya: noticing a correlated pattern: node-4 shows burst of expired connections ~14:01. I suspect compaction job caused many small deletions and triggered eviction fallback which overloaded the replication path. Will check compaction logs.

liz: compaction logs show an error loop where compaction was repeatedly restarting due to an internal GC race. snippet:
```
compaction: start shard=12
compaction: error: goroutine panic: index-corrupt? retrying
compaction: retry count=7
```

alex: if compaction is corrupted we should stop compaction, revert to last stable config, and trigger a safe compact off-peak. For now keep bypass and TTL longer. Also consider enabling a soft-fallback route: if kv read fails, gateway should fallback to model-variant 'small-latency' rather than return 502.

jamal: agree. I'll coordinate rollback of compaction config and schedule a safe run off-peak. handing primary ownership to maya for postmortem and root-cause. I'm going offline for next 30m for a briefing, but will remain reachable. @maya you own the oncall for 2h.

maya: taking over. will collect logs, open incident page, assign follow-ups: (1) compaction race fix, (2) add circuit breaker, (3) tighten prefetch schedules, (4) add more robust read-through fallback and route-level throttles. Creating postmortem ticket: PM-INC-20260315.

emily-cs: customers notified. sending status update: "Investigating elevated errors; temporary routing change applied to reduce impact; engineering working on root cause. Will update in 30m." Sending that now.

liz: metrics now: 5xx = 0.9% (rolling 5m), p95 latency = 680ms. kv-store CPU rose by 12% but within safety. Eviction_count stable ~900/min.

ops-runner: will keep bypass at 25% for 20m, then iterate down if stable.

sre-bot: automated note: incident page created -> https://incidents.internal/2712345678

jamal: thanks team. handoff complete. maya owns incident now. leaving a small checklist for postmortem and customer follow-ups.

maya: will run deeper heap/profile on prefix-cache nodes and coordinate with infra for a safe compaction fix. tagging eng for a code fix for compaction retry loop.

alex: agreed to prepare a hotfix branch to hard-stop compaction retries while maintaining availability. will open PR and link to postmortem.

emily-cs: closing loop with Acme & NumiAI: they got our 1st update, will follow up with RCA when available. no new SEV pages requested at this time.

maya: updating incident status: mitigation effective, continuing investigation. will update thread with timeline and RCA later.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: MITIGATION: 5xx rate under threshold, canary bypass and TTL bump reduced eviction storm. Incident severity lowered to SEV2. Postmortem assigned.

jamal: handing off final notes: incident->maya, postmortem owner->maya, customer comms->emily-cs, follow-ups assigned to alex (hotfix), liz (metrics alert tuning), ops-runner (route control playbooks). closing active paging for now.

maya: closing oncall handoff. Will mark incident resolved once hotfix deployed and compaction fix validated. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
